newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy govt hopes to make metalworkers offer by Sat.
newsitem.headline: Italy govt hopes to make metalworkers offer by Sat.

text.p: Italian Labour Minister Tiziano Treu said on Thursday he hoped to be able to submit a proposal to metalworkers by Saturday to end a bitter dispute over contracts.
"By Saturday, I hope to be able to make a proposal," Treu told reporters ahead of a meeting with engineering and metal workers' unions and employers' association Federmeccanica.

Leaders from Italy's three main trades union confederations met Prime Minister Romano Prodi earlier for a first round of talks. Treu, finance minister Vincenzo Visco and industry minister Pier Luigi Bersani were also present at that meeting.

Unions representing 1.7 million workers in the metalworking and engineering sector, which accounts for about 40 percent of total manufacturing output in Italy, are locked in dispute with management over pay increases for the 1996-1998 period.
Metalworkers' contracts expired in June and unions have recently held two national strikes in support of their claims for wage rises.
